evidence: Every edge sits on one pixel grid (about 180 art pixels across the width): pixel art scaled up by an exact factor
Hundreds of identical sprites (green nuclei, pink and blue fragments, small neutron dots) placed on a regular lattice and moving by rule: a particle simulation, not hand animation
Counter panel ticks through exact powers of two in a bitmap font: generated, not typed by hand
shots.description: Pixel-art particle simulation on a near-black blue-tinted ground. Title "NUCLEAR FISSION" in a white bitmap font over one big glowing green nucleus (a cluster of small green balls with a soft dark-green halo), label U-235 under it, a tiny white neutron streaks in from the left. The nucleus splits into a pink (BA) and a blue (KR) nucleus that fly apart, firing 2-3 neutron dots. The view pulls back to a regular lattice of small green nuclei (each a 3-tone pixel ball, highlight top-left). A caption panel at the top and a counter panel under it (dark navy fill, 1 art-pixel green-tinted border, small corner ticks) show GENERATION n and a big splits count that doubles every half second (8, 64, 1,024, 131,072, then scientific notation 4.4x10^12 ... 6.0x10^23). Each split spawns pink and blue fragments; the lattice fills with fragment dots, a ring of orange-rimmed reacting nuclei spreads outward, and finally a dark-red then orange pixel fireball grows out of the middle.

narrative.point: Opens on one atom and a title, then shows a chain reaction doubling on a live counter until it explodes

evidence: Same pixel grid and counter panel as shot 1
Fireball made of flat pixel blobs in a 4-step orange-to-cream ramp brightening over 1.5 s
shots.description: The pixel fireball fills the frame and brightens through red, orange, amber and cream to almost white, with lighter pixel blobs boiling inside; the panels show 80 GENERATIONS IN ABOUT 1 MICROSECOND and 6.0x10^23 SPLITS, then fade as the frame whites out.

narrative.point: The microscopic count turns into a real explosion: the frame burns to white

evidence: A flat white frame for half a second
shots.description: Pure white flash hold (about 0.5 s) between the micro and macro worlds.

narrative.point: A white flash bridges the atom scale and the real-world scale

evidence: Sky built from 5 flat horizontal bands with stepped (dithered) edges, ground with scattered single dark pixels: hand-built pixel-art scene layers
Cloud is a stack of pixel puff circles in 3-4 brown tones growing and billowing smoothly: likely procedural puffs, possibly hand-drawn pixel animation
shots.description: Wide pixel-art desert at dusk: dark brown ground with black speckle pixels, a low purple mountain silhouette, a sky of 5 horizontal violet-to-indigo bands with stepped edges and a few star pixels. A small white-hot dome flashes on the horizon, a flat light ring races out along the ground, the dome swells into an orange fireball with a purple rim, then rises on a stem into a brown mushroom cloud made of round pixel puffs (3-4 brown tones, lighter on top, glowing red underside). A dark checkerboard-dithered shadow passes over the scene once. Caption panels at the top (dark navy fill, 1 art-pixel dusty-rose border): TRINITY TEST, 1945 / FIRST ATOMIC BOMB; PLUTONIUM FISSION 20,000+ TONS OF TNT; THE CLOUD ROSE 12 KM HIGH; ABOUT 1 GRAM OF MASS BECAME ENERGY (the big number in a larger font). Near the end the sunset glows orange-pink on the right horizon and a small sparkle twinkles on the cloud edge, then the camera starts to push in on it.

narrative.point: The real-world result, as three big stat cards over one growing image

evidence: Pixels get bigger as the view zooms: the whole pixel-art frame is scaled up, so the push-in is a scale of the rendered scene
shots.description: Fast push-in toward the sparkle on the cloud edge: the cloud fills the frame with chunky enlarged pixels and the sparkle grows into a bright cream-orange glow disc that fills the frame.

narrative.point: A push-in into a point of light carries the viewer back to the atom

evidence: Match cut on a round bright shape; the green nucleus enlarged with big pixels then shown at normal size: the same sprite as shot 1
shots.description: Match cut from the glow disc to an extreme close-up of the green nucleus (huge pixel balls), which pulls back to the opening frame: title NUCLEAR FISSION and the U-235 nucleus on the dark ground, so the video loops seamlessly.

narrative.point: Ends on its own first frame so the reel loops

editing.editing: Almost one continuous take per world: 18 s micro simulation, white flash, 22 s macro scene, push-in and match cut to loop; captions change about every 3-5 s

format.format: Silent-text explainer: no voice-over, music plus sound effects, all information in on-screen caption panels and counters

style.render_style: Pixel art at a low fixed resolution (about 180 x 320 art pixels, scaled up by an exact factor), drawn and animated in code; retro game look
style.outline: No dark outlines; shapes are separated by colour steps. UI panels have a 1-art-pixel border in a muted tint of the scene colour
style.shading: Flat fills in 3-4 step colour ramps (shadow, base, light, highlight); light from the top-left on spheres and cloud puffs; hot things glow through a red-orange-amber-cream ramp; skies are flat horizontal bands with stepped edges; dark overlays use checkerboard dithering
style.shape_language: Round and chunky: balls and puff clusters built from pixel circles, low flat horizon lines, silhouettes readable at tiny size; subjects small inside a big field of repeated elements, or one big subject on a wide simple scene
style.texture: Hard pixel edges everywhere, scattered single-pixel specks on the ground, star pixels in the sky, checkerboard dither for passing shadows; no noise, no blur, no smooth gradients
style.type_ui: Uppercase monospace bitmap (pixel) font in near-white; caption panel at the top centre (dark navy fill, 1-pixel border tinted to the scene); a second counter panel under it with GENERATION n, a large number, a unit line and small corner ticks; numbers switch to scientific notation (6.0x10^23 with superscript) when large; short labels (U-235) right under objects
style.motion_style: Rule-driven simulation (particles split, fly, multiply on a lattice) with a counter ticking every 0.5 s; growth effects (fireball swells, cloud rises and billows); a full-frame white flash between scale levels; one push-in at the end and a match cut back to the first frame for a seamless loop; motion is smooth but positions snap to the pixel grid
style.signature: Low-res pixel grid on everything; near-black space ground with one bright sprite colour; HUD panels with bitmap font and live counters; micro-to-macro story with a white flash bridge; ends on its own first frame (loop)
style.do_not_copy: The @BITWONDER watermark under the counter, the exact topic (nuclear fission, uranium, Trinity test, mushroom cloud) and its numbers

story.summary: A 44 s pixel-art explainer that shows nuclear fission as a game-like chain reaction with a live counter, then jumps to the real explosion it causes, with no narration: music, sound effects and short HUD captions carry it.
story.hook: 0-3 s: a big bold title and one glowing nucleus on black, a neutron already flying at it; the viewer knows something is about to happen.
highlights: 8-17 s: a counter doubles every half second (8, 64, 1,024 ... 6.0x10^23) while the screen fills with sprites: exponential growth you can watch, numbers that escalate faster than you can read
17-20 s: the count literally becomes fire and burns to white: the climax lands as one image, then a hard switch from atom scale to real-world scale
20-42 s: one growing image (the cloud) under 3 short stat cards (20,000+ tons, 12 km, 1 gram): each stat lands while the picture is still changing
42-44 s: push into a glint and match-cut to the first frame: the reel loops, so viewers watch it twice
